calm.name: Stress Relief
calm.subtitle: Classic 4–6 breathing pattern
calm.description: Sometimes tension takes over, and we just need a pause to catch our breath. This practice is designed as your personal “reset button.” It gently soothes the nervous system, helping you let go of anxiety and regain a clear mind.
calm.fullDescription: The “4-6” breathing pattern uses 10-second cycles for quick stress relief. A 4-second inhale flows smoothly, without pauses, into a 6-second exhale with a deep release. This extended exhale stimulates the vagus nerve, slowing your heart rate and helping to lower cortisol levels.
calm.final_text: You’ve given yourself a precious minute of silence. May this gentle sense of peace and relaxation stay with you for as long as possible.

square.name: Focus
square.subtitle: “4-4-4-4” Box Breathing
square.description: Box breathing is a reliable anchor during stress or when you feel out of control. The steady rhythm of inhales, exhales, and gentle pauses creates a sense of stability. Just follow the prompts: each cycle step-by-step releases tension, grounds you, and restores mental clarity.
square.fullDescription: The symmetrical “4-4-4-4” pattern stabilizes the nervous system and improves concentration. Each cycle consists of equal 4-second phases: inhale, hold, exhale, and pause. Breath holds help regulate carbon dioxide levels and lower your heart rate, while the steady rhythm helps you maintain focus and restore balance.
square.final_text: You’ve regained your balance and focus. Take a deep breath, a light smile — and you’re ready to take on your day.

deep_relax.name: Deep Relaxation
deep_relax.subtitle: The “4-2-6” breathing pattern
deep_relax.description: When the day has been long and tension has built up in the body, this practice helps you gently settle and come back to yourself. A brief pause after the inhale gives the mind a moment to quiet down, while the longer exhale brings a deeper sense of release. It’s an ideal choice for easing muscle fatigue and winding down in the evening.
deep_relax.fullDescription: The “4-2-6” pattern uses 12-second cycles for deep relaxation. A smooth 4-second inhale leads into a short 2-second pause at the peak. The cycle concludes with a long, gentle 6-second exhale. This structure helps physiologically relieve muscle tension and shifts the nervous system into rest mode.
deep_relax.final_text: The tension has eased, making room for softness and calm. Stay with this feeling a little longer, and allow yourself the rest you deserve.

reset.name: Reset
reset.subtitle: The “2-1-6” breathing pattern
reset.description: Sometimes the body feels stuck in tension: breathing becomes shallow, thoughts race, and you feel overwhelmed. This practice helps you perform a gentle reset. A double inhale fills your lungs slightly deeper, while the long exhale helps release excess tension and brings you back to yourself.
reset.fullDescription: The “2-1-6” pattern is based on a gentle physiological sigh. First, you take a calm 2-second inhale, followed by a small 1-second additional inhale, and then a long, slow 6-second exhale. This rhythm helps deepen your breathing, relieves the feeling of tightness in your chest, and gradually shifts you from tension to a calmer, clearer state.
reset.final_text: You’ve taken a pause and helped your body release excess tension. Allow yourself a few more seconds to simply exist in this new, lighter state.

balance.name: Balance
balance.subtitle: Steady “5-5” breathing
balance.description: Sometimes, you don’t need to force relaxation or strive for deep calm—you just need to steady your internal rhythm. This practice helps you gently slow down, regain stability, and reconnect with yourself. Equal inhales and exhales create a calm, predictable pace that is easy to follow.
balance.fullDescription: The “5-5” breathing pattern uses 10-second cycles without pauses. A 5-second inhale flows smoothly into an equal 5-second exhale. This steady rhythm helps stabilize your breathing, reduce internal restlessness, and restore a sense of calm control without unnecessary tension.
balance.final_text: You’ve steadied your breathing and given yourself a few minutes of stability. May this calm sense of balance stay with you as you continue your day.
